subject.title: Adding ACP agent to agents.list silently hijacks all routing from implicit main agent

question: Should OpenClaw continue allowing the first `agents.list` entry to become the default implicitly, or require/prompt for an explicit default when existing `main` state could be displaced?
rationale: The viable fixes intentionally change routing semantics, warning behavior, or config-write UX, and automation should not choose that product/security contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Require explicit default on first listed-agent setup
options.body: Make config-write/setup/doctor flows stop or prompt when a first non-empty `agents.list` has no `default: true` and existing `main` state would be displaced.

options.title: Warn but preserve first-entry fallback
options.body: Keep runtime behavior compatible while adding high-visibility warning plus docs/doctor guidance for first-time listed-agent configs.

options.title: Auto-preserve `main` when state exists
options.body: Materialize or prefer `main` as default when previous `main` state exists, protecting continuity but changing first-entry-only config meaning.

recommendation.title: Require explicit default on first listed-agent setup
recommendation.body: Make config-write/setup/doctor flows stop or prompt when a first non-empty `agents.list` has no `default: true` and existing `main` state would be displaced.

likelyOwner.reason: The default-agent routing behavior originated in Peter Steinberger's multi-agent routing work and the current implementation is still most strongly tied to that history.
